companyDescription: Rockets, spacecraft & lunar landers · first commercial firm to complete a successful Moon landing (Blue Ghost) · Q2 2026 revenue up 659% YoY to a record $117.7M — the fundamentals/sentiment divergence flagged last report has genuinely started closing
priceNote: Self-fetched today (live-prices.json cache dated Aug 13, too stale to use). Up 13.6% since the last report ($20.65 → $23.45) after Q2 2026 results (Aug 11) delivered record revenue of $117.7M, up 659% YoY — a genuine acceleration from Q1's 45% YoY pace that the last report specifically flagged as the thing to watch.
summary: This is a genuinely positive update, but with an important honest caveat: the fundamentals/sentiment divergence flagged last report has started closing (stock +13.6% since July), and Q2 2026 revenue exploded to $117.7M (+659% YoY) with FY26 guidance raised to $420-450M — a real inflection, not just noise. New contract wins keep landing (SSC Space multi-launch deal, NASA Spacecraft Processing Contract, Space Force $93.7M radar digitization, a new cleanroom for 12-unit simultaneous Blue Ghost/Elytra production). BUT the 10-analyst consensus target has fallen to $38.6 (+64.6%) from $48.11 last report, and the high estimate is now $50 (+113%) versus Roth's prior $60 (+191%) — the stock's own rally has compressed the remaining upside below this board's typical 200%+ turbo floor even further than before. Cash is strong ($635.2M total liquidity). Next earnings Nov 11, 2026 is the catalyst that tests whether $420-450M FY guidance holds.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Reports Nov 11, 2026. Tests whether the raised FY26 guidance ($420-450M revenue) holds after Q2's 659% YoY beat. Market will also want an update on the SSC Space and NASA processing contract cadence.

catalysts.name: New Cleanroom — Production Scale-Up
catalysts.description: ISO Class 8 cleanroom completed in Cedar Park, TX (Sep 22), enabling simultaneous assembly of up to 12 Blue Ghost lunar landers and Elytra orbital vehicles — direct evidence the company is building out capacity to match its expanding contract backlog.

catalysts.name: Contract Momentum — SSC Space, NASA, Space Force
catalysts.description: Multi-launch deal with SSC Space (Alpha rocket launches from Sweden, 2028+), NASA Spacecraft Processing Operations Contract (Vandenberg payload processing), and SciTec's $93.7M Space Force radar digitization contract — real, diversified revenue visibility beyond the original Blue Ghost/SkyFall wins.

risks: Real upside has compressed further below this board's 200%+ turbo bar — the 10-analyst consensus fell to $38.6 (+64.6%) from $48.11 last report, and even the new high estimate ($50, +113%) is below Roth's prior $60 (+191%). The stock's own rally is eating the remaining asymmetry faster than the fundamentals story is expanding it
FY26 guidance of $420-450M implies a steep H2 ramp from the $117.7M Q2 print — Nov 11 earnings is a real test of execution, not just a formality
Net loss was $92.3M in Q2 despite the revenue beat — still cash-burning at scale even as growth accelerates
Most new contract wins (SSC Space 2028+, Space Force radar work) are multi-year — cash doesn't flow immediately even as backlog visibility improves
This is now a genuinely borderline turbo pick on a strict upside basis — worth flagging for the next `turbo-compare` cycle rather than treating the Moon case here as a clean 200%+ moonshot

macroRisk.sectorImpact: The space sector's sentiment has stabilized somewhat since the last report as Firefly's own fundamentals started catching up to the news flow, but the sector remains sensitive to broad risk-off moves and capital rotation (e.g. toward SpaceX's IPO).
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — Firefly's contract wins are macro-independent, but the stock's re-rating this quarter shows it's still exposed to broad growth-stock rate sensitivity, same as its eVTOL/space peers.
